title: Kedah-Perlis District
capsule: Siam separated the small principality of Perlis from Kedah in 1843 following the restoration of the Sultan of Kedah, installing Sayyid Hussain Jamalullail — of Hadrami Arab descent — as its first Raja on 20 May 1843 under direct Bangkok suzerainty. The Jamalullail dynasty presided over a rice-growing territory on the Thai-Malay frontier while acknowledging the Siamese king as overlord; Siam intervened on Perlis's behalf against a Kedah annexation attempt in 1897. The Anglo-Siamese Treaty of 1909 required Siam to transfer Perlis, Kedah, Kelantan, and Terengganu to British protection, ending roughly 66 years of Siamese suzerainty.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Administrative boundaries are reasonably well documented from Siamese and British survey records; the dataset label conflates Kedah and Perlis, reflecting their pre-1843 union and contested borderland status.
